method: Volumes are converted to millilitres using 1 US cup = 236.5882365 mL and 1 L = 1000 mL. For starting volume Vi, current measured volume Vc, target reduction p percent and elapsed steady-simmer time e minutes, the target volume is Vf = Vi × (1 − p/100), the observed loss is Vi − Vc, and the measured average evaporation rate is r = (Vi − Vc)/e. If Vc is above Vf, liquid left to evaporate is Vc − Vf, estimated remaining time is (Vc − Vf)/r, and total trial-plus-remaining time is e plus that result. At or below Vf, remaining volume and time are zero. Actual reduction is (Vi − Vc)/Vi × 100. The approximate retained-solute concentration multiplier is Vi/Vf. Volumes are rounded to 0.1 mL, rate to 0.01 mL/min, percentages to 0.1 point, times to 0.1 minute and multiplier to 0.01 for catalog comparisons; display rounds to practical kitchen precision. Starting volume accepts 30–10000 mL, 0.03–10 L or 0.125–42 US cups; current volume must be positive and below the start, target is 1–95 percent and elapsed time is 1–1440 minutes. The time estimate deliberately uses the user’s measured trial rather than an assumed burner or pan rate. It assumes a constant rate and retained dissolved ingredients; heat, exposed surface, lid position, solids and viscosity can invalidate that assumption. It does not predict texture, flavour, saltiness or food safety.
